thread:
Ava: quick follow-up from the design review — there's a discussion about quantization of the min/max slider steps. people asking for both fine-grained control and quicker large jumps. thoughts?
Ravi: current slider step = 1 GPU. issue: to go from 1->32 is tedious. but coarse steps risk overshooting for low-cost workloads.
Maya: UX idea: dual-mode slider. default is fine mode (step=1). add a toggle or long-press to switch to coarse mode (step=4 or 8). show a small hint under the slider: 'Hold to jump faster'.
Noor: accessibility: long-press is hard for keyboard users. expose explicit modifiers: Shift+Drag or Shift+Arrow for +4 steps, Alt+Arrow for +8. Document aria-describedby that lists the modifiers.
Leo: implementation: slider supports variable step function: step = (modifier==shift ? 4 : modifier==alt ? 8 : 1). For drag acceleration use delta-based math to snap to nearest step. I'll prototype.
Ava: what about a visible affordance so people discover the modifiers? maybe a micro affordance near the slider that says 'Quick jump: Shift/Alt'.
Ravi: prefer a subtle persistent hint (small text) rather than changing label. also show an animated micro-toast when modifier detected: 'Jump mode: +4'.
Maya: micro-copy: hint text should be short: 'Shift/Alt to jump'. tooltip expands: 'Shift: +4, Alt: +8'. keep it readable on mobile (show long-press guidance).
Noor: SR announcement: when a user crosses a guardrail (e.g., max > 12) announce: 'Warning: high capacity may increase cost; see guardrails'. For jump mode changes announce: 'Jump mode activated: +4'. Use aria-live polite.
Ravi: another ask: allow pinning a default pool per project in the SLO card. saves a click for teams that always use the same pool. should be opt-in.
Leo: backend note: pinning requires storing project preferences; I'll add an endpoint `POST /api/projects/:id/prefs` with {default_pool_id}. low risk but needs migration.
Ava: UI: add a tiny pin icon inside the pool dropdown with text 'Pin default'. if pinned, show a subtle pin badge on the pool chip. also add an undo toast when pin changed.
Maya: accessibility: pin toggle must be keyboard reachable and announced: 'Pinned as default for this project'. Link to 'Manage defaults' in the picker for advanced settings.
Noor: color/accessibility nit: pool badges use colored outlines. ensure outline contrast meets 3:1 with background and provide an icon fallback (pool initials) so color isn't the only differentiator.
Ava: final UX question: burst enable still prompts a confirmation for first-time enable on project only. should we keep modal or switch to inline admonition that requires typing 'ENABLE'?
Ravi: modal with a single confirm button is lightweight. typing 'ENABLE' is safer but slows down incident response. maybe require typing only for account-level toggles, not project-level.
Leo: we can track the first-time enable at project scope. modal with a checkbox 'Don't show again for this project' is a good compromise. store preference in prefs endpoint.
Maya: microtest plan: 1) slider jump modifiers: use keyboard and mouse to change values 2) pin default pool and verify undo toast 3) enable burst first-time modal and toggle 'Don't show again' 4) verify SR announcements and tab order. 3 engineers, 15 mins.
design-bot: created branch feature/slider-jump-pin-pool-231999 and uploaded mock sliders_pin_pool.png
Ava: thanks all. Leo, please attach prototype screenshots. Noor, once the branch is up can you run the SR/keyboard pass and post findings here?
Noor: will do. will verify aria-live, modifier announcements, and color contrast. reporting back Friday.
Ava: perfect. closing this thread and moving notes into the product spec. :rocket:
